task_description: You're importing createReactAgent from '@langchain/langgraph/prebuilts' to build an agent. In LangChain JS v1 the function was moved and renamed. Update the import and function call.
deprecated_pattern:
import { createReactAgent } from '@langchain/langgraph/prebuilts';
const agent = createReactAgent({ model, tools, prompt: 'You are helpful' });
correct_pattern:
import { createAgent } from 'langchain';
const agent = createAgent({ model, tools, systemPrompt: 'You are helpful' });
why_models_fail_this: createReactAgent from @langchain/langgraph/prebuilts was the recommended agent builder throughout the LangGraph prebuilt era (0.2+). Models produce this import path and the old 'prompt' parameter automatically. The rename to createAgent in langchain and the parameter rename to systemPrompt are both unknown to pre-v1 models.

task_description: You're passing a system prompt to a LangChain agent using the 'prompt' parameter. In v1 this parameter was renamed. Fix the call.
deprecated_pattern: createReactAgent({ model, tools, prompt: 'You are a helpful assistant' })
correct_pattern: createAgent({ model, tools, systemPrompt: 'You are a helpful assistant' })
why_models_fail_this: The 'prompt' parameter was the documented system prompt option in createReactAgent throughout the LangGraph 0.2+ era and appears in all official agent examples. Models produce it reflexively. The rename to systemPrompt in createAgent is not predictable from context.

task_description: After upgrading to LangChain JS v0.3, your code breaks because @langchain/core types don't match. What changed about how @langchain/core must be installed?
deprecated_pattern:
// Only install langchain and provider packages; @langchain/core resolved transitively
// package.json: { "dependencies": { "langchain": "^0.3", "@langchain/openai": "^0.3" } }
correct_pattern:
// @langchain/core must be an explicit peer/direct dependency in package.json
// package.json: { "dependencies": { "langchain": "^0.3", "@langchain/openai": "^0.3", "@langchain/core": "^0.3" } }
why_models_fail_this: Before v0.3, @langchain/core was a direct dependency of langchain and resolved transitively. The shift to a peer dependency requires explicit installation, which models don't know about and cannot infer from import statements alone.

task_description: In a serverless function (Vercel, AWS Lambda), your LangSmith traces are incomplete after upgrading to v0.3. Callbacks are now non-blocking by default. What must you do to ensure traces finish before the function returns?
deprecated_pattern:
const result = await chain.invoke(input);
return Response.json({ result }); // callbacks may not complete
why_models_fail_this: Before v0.3, callbacks were blocking and always completed before the function returned. The switch to non-blocking by default in v0.3 is a silent behavioral change that breaks tracing in serverless environments. Models have no training signal for awaitAllCallbacks() since it was introduced to address this new default.

task_description: You're importing LLMChain from 'langchain/chains'. In LangChain JS v1 this module no longer exists in the main package. Where should you import it from?
why_models_fail_this: langchain/chains was a stable subpath for LLMChain, ConversationChain, and other chains throughout all of LangChain JS v0. The introduction of @langchain/classic as a separate package for legacy functionality in v1 is entirely new and unknown to models trained before the release.

task_description: You're using preModelHook in createReactAgent to trim messages before model calls. In LangChain JS v1 this hook was replaced. Rewrite it using the v1 approach.
correct_pattern:
import { summarizationMiddleware } from 'langchain';
createAgent({ model, tools, middleware: [summarizationMiddleware({ model, trigger: { tokens: 1000 } })] })
why_models_fail_this: preModelHook was documented in LangGraph JS examples as the way to intercept and modify messages before model calls. The middleware system introduced in v1 is a completely different abstraction. Models trained before v1 have no knowledge of summarizationMiddleware or the middleware pattern.

task_description: You're passing runtime configuration to an agent using config.configurable. In LangChain JS v1 the recommended pattern changed. Update the agent invocation.
why_models_fail_this: config.configurable was the standard mechanism for passing runtime config through LangChain and LangGraph runnables throughout v0. Models produce it reflexively when injecting user-specific context. The new context parameter in createAgent is a v1-specific pattern.

task_description: You're streaming events from a LangChain agent and filtering for events from the 'agent' node to display intermediate steps. In v1 this node name changed. Update the filter.
why_models_fail_this: The 'agent' node name for the LLM call node was used in all LangGraph streaming examples throughout v0. Filtering for this node name in streamEvents is a documented pattern. The rename to 'model' in v1 is a subtle breaking change that silently returns no events.

task_description: You're sending an image to a multimodal model using the OpenAI-style content array with 'image_url' type. In LangChain JS v1 there is a new provider-agnostic way to do this. Update the message construction.
deprecated_pattern: new HumanMessage({ content: [{ type: 'text', text: 'Describe this' }, { type: 'image_url', image_url: { url: 'https://example.com/img.png' } }] })
correct_pattern: new HumanMessage({ contentBlocks: [{ type: 'text', text: 'Describe this' }, { type: 'image', url: 'https://example.com/img.png' }] })
why_models_fail_this: The OpenAI-style content array with 'image_url' was the standard way to build multimodal messages in LangChain JS throughout v0. It is deeply ingrained in training data. The new contentBlocks API with a simplified 'image' type (no nested object) is a v1 abstraction that models have no prior knowledge of.

task_description: You're using ToolNode with handleToolErrors option inside createReactAgent to catch tool execution errors. In LangChain JS v1 this was replaced. Update the tool error handling approach.
deprecated_pattern:
import { createReactAgent, ToolNode } from '@langchain/langgraph/prebuilts';
const agent = createReactAgent({ model, tools: new ToolNode(tools, { handleToolErrors: true }) });
why_models_fail_this: ToolNode with handleToolErrors was the documented mechanism for graceful tool error handling in LangGraph JS. It appears in official LangGraph examples. The replacement via wrapToolCall middleware in v1 is a fundamentally different API that pre-v1 models cannot predict.

task_description: You're using responseFormat with a plain Zod schema in createReactAgent to get structured output. In LangChain JS v1 you must explicitly choose a strategy. Update the structured output configuration.
correct_pattern:
import { toolStrategy } from 'langchain';
createAgent({ model, tools, responseFormat: toolStrategy(OutputSchema) })
why_models_fail_this: Passing a Zod schema directly to responseFormat in createReactAgent was the documented structured output approach. In v1, you must explicitly choose toolStrategy or providerStrategy. Models produce the plain schema pattern and have no knowledge of the toolStrategy wrapper.

task_description: You're passing a function to the prompt parameter in createReactAgent to implement a dynamic system prompt that adapts based on state. In v1 this was replaced. Show the v1 equivalent.
deprecated_pattern: createReactAgent({ model, tools, prompt: (state) => `You serve ${state.context.userRole} users` })
correct_pattern:
import { dynamicSystemPromptMiddleware } from 'langchain';
createAgent({ model, tools, middleware: [dynamicSystemPromptMiddleware((_state, runtime) => `You serve ${runtime.context.userRole} users`)], contextSchema })
why_models_fail_this: Passing a function to prompt in createReactAgent for dynamic system prompts was a documented LangGraph pattern. The replacement with dynamicSystemPromptMiddleware in v1 is a completely different abstraction. Models produce the function-as-prompt pattern and have no training signal for the middleware approach.

task_description: After upgrading to LangChain JS v1, imports from 'langchain/chains' and 'langchain/retrievers' fail with module not found errors. What package must you install and what do you update imports to?
deprecated_pattern:
import { RetrievalQAChain } from 'langchain/chains';
import { MultiQueryRetriever } from 'langchain/retrievers/multi-query';
correct_pattern:
import { RetrievalQAChain } from '@langchain/classic/chains';
import { MultiQueryRetriever } from '@langchain/classic/retrievers/multi-query';
why_models_fail_this: langchain/chains and langchain/retrievers/... subpath imports were stable documented entrypoints throughout all of LangChain JS v0. The complete removal from the main package and migration to @langchain/classic is unknown to models trained before v1.

task_description: You're reading reasoning/thinking content from a model response by iterating over response.content and checking for provider-specific types like 'thinking' or 'reasoning'. In LangChain JS v1 there is a provider-agnostic API for this. Update the code.
why_models_fail_this: Provider-specific content block parsing (checking for 'thinking' on Anthropic vs 'reasoning' on OpenAI) was the only way to handle reasoning content before v1. Models produce this provider-specific pattern. The unified contentBlocks API is a new v1 abstraction that models have no training data for.

task_description: You're passing a model pre-bound with tools to createAgent to control exactly which tools the model can call. In LangChain JS v1 pre-bound models are not supported in createAgent. How should you pass the model and tools?
deprecated_pattern:
const modelWithTools = new ChatOpenAI({ model: 'gpt-4o' }).bindTools([myTool]);
const agent = createAgent({ model: modelWithTools, tools: [] });
correct_pattern: const agent = createAgent({ model: new ChatOpenAI({ model: 'gpt-4o' }), tools: [myTool] });
why_models_fail_this: model.bindTools() was a common LangChain JS pattern for explicitly controlling which tools a model can use, and was used with createReactAgent in some examples. The restriction against pre-bound models in createAgent is a v1-specific constraint that models trained before the release will not know about.

task_description: You're instantiating a ChatOpenAI model directly with the provider class and then hard-coding it. In modern LangChain JS there is a provider-agnostic way to initialize any chat model from a string. Use it instead.
deprecated_pattern:
import { ChatOpenAI } from '@langchain/openai';
const model = new ChatOpenAI({ model: 'gpt-4o' });
correct_pattern:
import { initChatModel } from 'langchain';
const model = await initChatModel('gpt-4o', { modelProvider: 'openai' });
why_models_fail_this: Directly instantiating provider-specific classes like ChatOpenAI was the universal pattern throughout LangChain JS v0 and appears in virtually all documentation. initChatModel for provider-agnostic initialization was added later and is rarely seen in pre-0.2 training data.

task_description: You're adding custom state to a LangChain agent by passing a state schema directly to createReactAgent. In v1 custom state is defined via middleware. Rewrite this for v1.
deprecated_pattern:
import { getCurrentTaskInput } from '@langchain/langgraph';
const agent = createReactAgent({ model, tools, stateSchema: z.object({ userName: z.string() }) });
why_models_fail_this: Passing stateSchema directly to createReactAgent was the documented way to add custom state in LangGraph JS throughout v0. Using getCurrentTaskInput() to read state in tools was the established pattern. The v1 middleware-based state definition is a new abstraction with a different API surface.
